Params: Getting in took longer than expected.
By now, the blue glow inside is faint.
Even so, that faint blue light feels unreal. The water no longer looks like ordinary seawater. It shines like a gem.
The reflections rippling across the rock walls almost look more like the real ocean.
The boat is floating on the surface, yet it feels as if you're deep under the sea.
There are many sea caves around this island, but this one is the most famous.
I heard that before the sea rose, you could still see traces of older human activity here.
It's only a hollow carved out by the sea, and yet it became something so beautiful.
If you hadn't invited me, Bianca, I would've missed this incredible sight.
I did have a personal reason for coming here.
I once watched a film about the sea.
The protagonist grew up by the ocean. Even after losing a loved one to the sea, they could never stop loving it.
Years later, the protagonist went diving with a close friend. An accident happened, and before dying, the friend asked to be buried at sea.
After that, the protagonist often dreamed of sinking to the ocean floor. He felt himself drifting farther and farther from human society.
There was always a hollow place in his heart. Maybe only the sea could fill it.
In the end, he gave up everything he once had. Only the sea could bring him peace.
I've always wondered what made diving feel so peaceful to him. Was that peace a kind of happiness? I thought this blue hole might help me understand.
The boat lurches violently. A strong jolt throws you both toward one side.
Water splashes up, followed by the sound of something falling into the sea.
Your sharp eyes catch what fell. They also catch the panic and loss in Bianca's eyes the moment she realizes it's gone.
But with the boat still rocking, she can't worry about it yet.
You react immediately, grabbing the oar before it can fall and using it to steady the boat.
Once the oar is secure, you suddenly dive into the water, sending up another splash.
It all happens too fast. Bianca realizes the boat may have struck a submerged rock or reef, but she doesn't understand why you jumped in.
Whatever the reason is, Bianca is already at the side of the boat.
A hand in the water stops her before she can dive in. You resurface almost immediately.
Part of the hull is caught on an underwater reef.
Commandant...! Please get back in the boat!
Why did you jump in without warning me? What if you'd been hurt? If you needed something, I could have—
Your voice pulls Bianca out of her daze. She lets out a quiet breath, though her brow remains furrowed.
...I'm sorry. I shouldn't have lost my composure.
But I still mean what I said. You shouldn't have jumped in like that.
But trust me. I knew what I was doing.
I do trust you, Commandant. Please come back aboard. So the reason you jumped...
Bianca leans over the boat's edge and reaches out to help. That's when she sees what you are holding.
The blue light of the cave shimmers in her eyes. Now she understands why you dove in.
You answer her outstretched hand in another way.
The starfish shell that fell into the sea is now tied around her wrist with the pale-gold byssus cord that had been around your neck.
Sea caves are formed by erosion. That's true.
But a hollow doesn't have to be filled only by seawater.
Just like this abandoned boat became home to a small new ecosystem by the shore.
This blue hole has its own ecosystem too.
And it's because there are cracks for light to enter that this cave looks the way it does now.
Bianca, the blue hole isn't lonely.
And I believe the protagonist can find happiness too.
Bianca's wrist is slender. You wrap the byssus cord around it a few times, making sure the starfish is secure.
There. It shouldn't fall off now.
I hope you don't mind that I was wearing it before.
Bianca stares at the simple new bracelet on her wrist, lost in thought.
Why would I mind? This... makes it even better.
With a gentle shake of your head, you swim to the bow instead, where the boat is wedged between two underwater rocks.
You push against the boat, trying to free it from the rocks.
But the boat is stuck tight. To free it without damaging the rocks or the hull, you will need to push from two directions at once.
Bianca's ivory hair and sheer fabric drift through the water, like a sea nymph from an old legend.
Working together, you finally free the boat.
After helping each other back into the boat, you look at each other, both soaked and a little disheveled, and can't help laughing.
Your time in the blue hole is nearly over.
You return the way you came. By the time you see the open sky again, the pink sunset has deepened into purple dusk.
I still ended up making you jump in too.
How could I let you handle that alone?
Without proper training, staying in the water too long can lead to hypothermia.
I trust your physical condition, Commandant, but I don't want you taking that kind of risk.
But... is it just me, or...
As you speak, the boat is heading toward the main island, but it's not staying on course.
It has also started to slow down.
That's why the boat keeps drifting whenever we row.
It must have happened when we hit the reef earlier.
At this rate, the trip back will take longer than the trip out.
The sky is getting darker, and the cool wind of the summer night begins to rise.
For both of you, already soaked through, the wind feels even colder.
It might get cold if we stay out much longer.
I'm worried you'll get cold, Bianca.
Are you cold, Commandant? I'll find a way to fix that.
The accident happened because I wasn't careful enough.
I was told: The warmth of two people together can overcome even the coldest of winters in this world.
Bianca pauses. Then the guilt on her face softens into a fond, wistful smile.
Yes... I once made it through a snowstorm because of the warmth we shared.
If that warmth can get us through a winter storm, it can get us through cold seawater and night wind too.
I don't want you catching a chill.
You shift closer and gently lean against Bianca's shoulder. Bianca lowers her cheek to your head, careful as though touching something fragile.
You should worry about yourself before worrying about me.
The accident happened because I wasn't careful enough.
I was told: The warmth of two people together can overcome even the coldest of winters in this world.
Bianca pauses. Then the guilt on her face softens into a fond, wistful smile.
Yes... I once made it through a snowstorm because of the warmth we shared.
If that warmth can get us through a winter storm, it can get us through cold seawater and night wind too.
If you're worried about me, then I'm allowed to worry about you. So...
May I lean on you too?
You lean in without a word. Bianca slowly, carefully rests against your shoulder, her breathing almost softer than before.
The warmth they share makes up for the heat the evening wind keeps stealing away.
After a while, Bianca lifts her head.
I wish this moment could last a little longer... but Commandant, the sun is almost down.
That singing in the distance... Is the evening festival about to begin?
I'm sorry. I invited you out here and ended up wasting so much of your time.
No one would call a journey like this a waste of time.
Besides, we're not too far from the main island now.
We may miss the opening, but we'll make it to the festival.
Neither of you is rowing, so the sound must have come from something in the water.
A triangular dorsal fin breaks the surface. You both tense, only for a familiar head to pop up after it.
This time, you understand the dolphin right away and row after it.
Soon, you see why the dolphin brought you here.
The water here seems to be pushing us toward shore.
An onshore current is a nearshore current that runs perpendicular to the coastline and flows toward shore.
You risked getting stranded just to lead us into a current that could carry us back?
Thank you... You really are a miracle.
Riding the onshore current, you move toward the coast much faster.
Before the singing ends, you finally make it back to land.
Villagers pass by in festival clothes, probably on their way to the celebration.
Two older villagers walking together stop in surprise when they see you and Bianca, both soaked.
Oh my, why are you two soaked through?
Did you fall into the sea? Quick, go get them a couple of towels. Big ones.
Thank you. We went to the blue hole.
You found the entrance without a local guide? Now that's something.
We met a... friend who was kind enough to show us the way.
Yes. We met a very kind friend out at sea.
All the locals are busy moving and getting ready for the festival. Who else could've shown you the way?
Well, maybe the Sea Spirit showed herself.
A brief splash comes from the shore, and the shadow of a dorsal fin slips into the dark sea.
You and Bianca exchange a glance, each reading the same thought in the other's eyes.
I did witness many miracles today.
A knowing smile crosses her lips. As the evening wind lifts her hair, Bianca gathers it back. On her raised wrist, the pale-gold bracelet glimmers softly.
